What NOT to translate: the scripted talk itself (SCRIPT lines in state.tsx) and VIDEO_TITLE. They represent what the speaker says / the video's own title, and captions are never translated in this product. Also keep the downloaded file name as is. Never translate "Heard", "YouTube", "Chrome".

"use client";

import { createContext, useCallback, useContext, useMemo, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { LOCALE_COOKIE, LOCALE_PARAM, type Locale } from "./config";
import { MESSAGES, type Messages } from "./messages";

interface I18nState {
  locale: Locale;
  setLocale: (next: Locale) => void;
}

const Ctx = createContext<I18nState | null>(null);

/** Holds the page language. The server picks the first one, so the page never flashes English. */
export function I18nProvider({ initialLocale, children }: { initialLocale: Locale; children: ReactNode }) {
  const [locale, setLocaleState] = useState<Locale>(initialLocale);

  const setLocale = useCallback((next: Locale) => {
    setLocaleState(next);
    document.documentElement.lang = next;
    document.cookie = `${LOCALE_COOKIE}=${next}; path=/; max-age=${60 * 60 * 24 * 365}; samesite=lax`;
    // A ?lang= in the address would override the new choice on reload, so drop it.
    const url = new URL(window.location.href);
    if (url.searchParams.has(LOCALE_PARAM)) {
      url.searchParams.delete(LOCALE_PARAM);
      window.history.replaceState(window.history.state, "", url);
    }
  }, []);

  const value = useMemo(() => ({ locale, setLocale }), [locale, setLocale]);
  return <Ctx.Provider value={value}>{children}</Ctx.Provider>;
}

export function useLocale(): I18nState {
  const v = useContext(Ctx);
  if (!v) throw new Error("useLocale must be used inside <I18nProvider>");
  return v;
}

/** The current language's words for one area of the site, e.g. `const t = useT("home"); t.hero.title`. */
export function useT<N extends keyof Messages>(namespace: N): Messages[N] {
  const { locale } = useLocale();
  return MESSAGES[locale][namespace];
}

content.text:
I translated the home page demo into all six languages, and `tsc --noEmit` passes with no errors. I have not looked at it in a browser, so whether the longer German and French words fit in the pill and popup is untested.

**Files changed**
- `/Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions/apps/web/src/i18n/messages/en/demo.ts` holds every English string exactly as it was, plus two small functions: `jumpTo(time)` and `seekValue(now, total)` for the seek bar's spoken value ("0:33 of 1:00").
- `/Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions/apps/web/src/i18n/messages/{es,fr,pt,de,ja}/demo.ts` are typed as `typeof en`, so they must have the same shape.
- In `/Users/rizelscarlett/Documents/agent-experiments/voice-experiments/live-captions/apps/web/src/components/hero-demo/`, these five files now use `useT("demo")`: `HeroDemo.tsx`, `ExtensionPopup.tsx`, `PlayerControls.tsx`, `TranscriptCard.tsx` and `VideoFrame.tsx`. That covers visible text, aria-labels and title tooltips: the demo group label, Listening/Not listening, Start/Stop captions, the popup texts, the CC, transcript and full-screen buttons, the transcript card, and play/pause, the badges and the seek bar on the player.
- I added `whitespace-nowrap` to the Start/Stop captions button, the popup's Live/Off status and the player's Live captions/Captions off badge. I changed no other layout classes.

**Short wording for the controls pill**
In most languages the Start/Stop button is shortened to fit the pill. The full meaning is still in the popup switch's label:

| | Start | Stop |
|---|---|---|
| es | "Subtitular" | "Detener" |
| fr | "Sous-titrer" | "Arrêter" |
| pt | "Legendar" | "Parar" |
| de | "Untertitel an" | "Untertitel aus" |
| ja | "字幕を開始" | "字幕を停止" |

German "Untertitel aus" is the longest. It should fit in the roughly 300px pill, but that's the first thing to check in the browser.

**Left in English, on purpose**
- The talk's lines in `SCRIPT` and `VIDEO_TITLE` ("Why curiosity matters"), because captions are never translated.
- The download file name `heard-transcript.txt`.
- "Heard", "YouTube", "Chrome" and "youtube.com".
- The German popup status reads "Live", which is the normal German word for it.

`state.tsx` and `icons.tsx` needed no changes.
